meta.title: 20 market crises and events: stocks, real estate, savings
meta.note: Figures were checked against the sources listed. A source URL marked verified=true appeared in real search results and its excerpt matched the figure. Videos are candidates found in search results: none was opened or watched. video=null means no reliable video was found.

text.en: On 9 March 2009 the S&P 500 closed at 676.53, down 56% from its October 2007 high. Twelve years later it was worth about 5.7 times as much.

source.name: AP / The Seattle Times – US bull market turns 9

sources.name: NBC News – Happy Seventh Birthday to Wall Street's Bull Market
NBC News – Market almost unrecognizable from a decade ago

text.en: After the fastest 30% drop in its history, the S&P 500 bottomed at 2,237.40 on 23 March 2020. It doubled in 354 trading days, the fastest doubling since WWII, helped by stimulus and the Fed.

source.name: CNBC – S&P 500 doubles from its pandemic bottom

sources.name: Axios – S&P 500 marks 100% gain from March 2020 low

video.title: S&P 500 doubles from its Covid low (354 days)
video.channel: Unknown (Dailymotion upload, content matches CNBC's story)

text.en: The S&P 500 fell about 5% in two sessions (2,000.56 on 27 June). Markets erased the loss within a week, and the index hit a record on 11 July 2016. The gain over the following six months was about 13% (our own calculation).

source.name: The Washington Post – Markets make up losses of Brexit within a week

sources.name: Reuters via Business Standard – US stocks drop for second day after Brexit vote
CNBC – Dow, S&P surge 3% for the week

video.title: Pound's shocking crash (about the pound, not the S&P 500)

text.en: The Dow fell 998.5 points (about 9%) within minutes, then recovered most of it. The session closed down about 3.2%, so the real gain was slim.

source.name: CNBC – The lasting impact of the 2010 flash crash

text.en: The Case-Shiller national index peaked in July 2006 (184.61) and bottomed in February 2012 (133.99, -27.4%). By early 2025 it stood about 141% above that low.

text.en: Ireland's property prices fell 54.4% from 2007 to 2013 (revised figure). From the early-2013 trough they rose 84.2% by December 2019.

text.en: Despite lockdowns, French existing-home prices rose 6.4% over 2020 and 7.1% over 2021 (Notaires-Insee index). A modest gain, but no crash.

source.name: INSEE – Notaires-Insee index, Q4 2021

sources.name: INSEE – Notaires-Insee index, Q4 2020

text.en: The Dow peaked at 381 in September 1929 and fell nearly 13% on Black Monday, 28 October. It lost about 89% by July 1932 and only regained its peak in November 1954.

source.name: Federal Reserve History – Stock Market Crash of 1929

sources.name: Risk Hub – The Wall Street Crash of 1929 (secondary; source of the -89% and 1954 figures)

video.title: Entrez dans l'Histoire – Le Krach de 1929 : la fin du rêve américain (Intégrale)

text.en: The Nasdaq plunged 78% in 31 months after its March 2000 peak. It only regained that record in April 2015, 15 years later. The S&P 500 lost about 49% (not independently sourced).

source.name: Bloomberg – Dot-Com Nightmare Is Over as Nasdaq Retakes Record Lost in 2000

text.en: The Dow lost 22.6% in a single session, a record. Less than two years later US stocks surpassed their pre-crash highs.

text.en: The S&P 500 sank 19.8% from its 20 September peak through Christmas Eve, on Fed rate hikes and trade-war fears. It rebounded from 26 December and erased the loss in spring 2019.

text.en: The Case-Shiller national index fell 27.4% from July 2006 to February 2012, and prices fell much further in the hardest-hit cities. More than 12.8 million homes entered foreclosure between 2007 and 2014.

text.en: The Livret A paid 3%, tax-free and capital-guaranteed, until 31 January 2025 after a government freeze. The real return was negative in 2023 (inflation near 5%) and turned positive in 2024.
